prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor retail space with a windowed wall on the right ( shifting to the center-right in frame 5) and a floor plane sloping away from the camera wearer. In frames 1 and 2, a seated man in a grey hoodie and tan pants is about 1.2–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer holding a patterned garment within his arm's reach, while a tablet on a counter at bottom right and a blurry foreground object in frame 2 sit within the camera wearer's arm's reach (under 0.8 m). As the camera pitches downward and turns left in frames 3 and 4, a red shopping basket and a person's head/arm at the bottom right are very bright (0.3–0.6 m, within the camera wearer's reach), the seated man's tan legs are 1.0–1.5 m to the right, hanging blue jeans on a rack are 1.2–1.8 m ahead in the center, and a standing person's legs are 2.0–2.5 m ahead to the left (about 0.5–1.0 m left of the jeans). In frame 5, the camera pans right and tilts up, placing the jeans rack 1.0–1.5 m to the left, the seated man 1.5–2.0 m to the lower right, and a lifted purple garment very bright at 0.3–0.6 m in the upper-right foreground occluding the window and part of the seated man. The depth map clarifies the continuous 3D separation between the foreground basket/garment, the mid-ground seated man and clothing rack, and the recessed window wall despite severe motion blur in frames 2 and 5, though it is unreliable on dark glass reflections (which appear artificially deep/black) and merges the seated man's held shirt seamlessly into his torso.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground entities against the unlabelled floor and walls across the camera's downward-and-left pan (frames 1–4) and rightward return (frame 5). In frames 1 and 2, the seated man facing and looking toward the camera wearer is segmented as a pink `person` mask at 1.2–1.5 m in the center-left, while the foreground occlusion on the right in frame 2 is labelled as a separate brown `person` mask within 0.8 m. In frames 3 and 4, where upper bodies are cropped out of view above the frame, the map separates three distinct regions from left to right: the standing person's legs at 2.0–2.5 m (pink `person`), the hanging blue jeans in the center at 1.2–1.8 m (yellow/cyan `person`), and the seated man's lower body and adjacent foreground occlusion on the right at 0.5–1.5 m (brown `person`), before tracking only the foreground lifted garment and seated man as a single pink `person` mask on the right in frame 5. This map makes it easier to distinguish overlapping foreground boundaries during heavy motion blur in frame 2, but it is highly unreliable across the strip: it misclassifies the right-hand window mullion and tablet in frame 1 as a `laptop`, the red shopping basket within the camera wearer's reach in frame 3 as a `chair`, and the hanging blue jeans in frames 3–4 as a `person`. Furthermore, it merges held garments (the patterned shirt in frames 1–2 and the foreground purple cloth in frame 5) into the `person` masks and completely misses the clothing rack on the left in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D skeletal keypoints for the seated man in frames 1, 2, and 5, while detecting no skeletons in frames 3 and 4 when only lower legs, the hanging jeans, and the top of a foreground head are in view. In frame 1, the yellow torso and limb skeleton shows the seated man 1.2–1.5 m ahead facing toward the camera wearer with his head tilted slightly down and eye/face keypoints directed toward the garment in his hands; both arms are bent within his arm's reach, with magenta hand keypoints clustered on his right hand gripping the hanger on the left side of the shirt. In frame 2, as the camera begins to pan and blur, his upper torso and right arm remain tracked in the same forward-facing posture while his left arm, left leg, and hand keypoints drop out due to motion blur and occlusion at the bottom right. In frame 5, after the camera pans back toward the right, a partial yellow skeleton appears in the lower right at 1.5–2.0 m showing his head and shoulders angled toward the left as the foreground purple garment occludes much of his body. The skeleton clearly reveals the seated man's shoulder orientation and elbow flexion behind the dark patterned cloth in frames 1 and 2, but it is unreliable in missing his left hand in frame 1, losing all hand and lower-body keypoints in frame 2, collapsing into a distorted cluster in frame 5 under occlusion, and failing to detect the visible legs of the people in frames 3 and 4.
